correctness.rationale: The graph and all 32 edges are specified. Every shortest path flips differing coordinates exactly once, so both independent generators enumerate every geodesic and its 3-edge subsets; both independently derive exactly 576 distinct forbidden triples. Legality is equivalent to avoiding them. The bitmask DFS invariant proves exhaustive generation without duplication, and terminal maximality is exactly absence of any legal single-edge augmentation. Independent Python BFS-layer path generation and cumulative valid-mask construction, then direct full-set maximality tests, reproduce all 17 face counts and seven nonzero facet counts. No extrapolation or unstated search cutoff; the claimed domain is only finite Q4.

value.rationale: Q4 is a canonical 16-vertex, 32-edge hypercube benchmark where the published general theorem fixes only maximum cardinality. The new complete simplex-face and facet polynomials reveal that minimal inclusion-maximal edge-general-position sets use just six edges while largest use sixteen, and exactly seven facet cardinalities occur with four internal missing sizes. This gives a substantive saturation/nonpurity boundary and exact benchmark for future small-dimensional and hypercube general-position questions; it is not an arbitrary labelled parameter slice or a recomputation of the known maximum alone.
